newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end slightly up amid profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end slightly up amid profit-taking.

text.p: Taiwan stocks failed to challenge the 7,000-point resistance and closed only slightly higher on Wednesday as waves of profit-taking eroded gains, brokers said.
The weighted index closed 5.19 points or a scant 0.07 percent higher at 6,932.96. Turnover shrank to T$89.80 billion from Tuesday's hectic turnover of T$104.37 billion.

The stock index briefly breached the 7,000-point resistance in early trade to rise to a 1996 intra-session high of 7,002.62, but selling pressure immediately emerged. "People feel the market has been over-heated in the short-term, it needs some time to cool," said Allen Huang of National securities.
Buying interest was scattered over various sectors' blue chip stocks, but the absence of leading sectors prevented an overall rally, brokers said.
Computer giant Acer Inc surged T$2 or 3.81 percent to T$54.5 and Yang Ming Marine gained T$1.6 or 4.60 percent to T$36.4.
Brokers noted persistent injections of new funds from investors who are dissatisfied with low bank interest rates helped the index at high levels.
"This is a liquidity-driven game and the bull run has not yet finished," said United Securities analyst Lin Long-hsien.
The performance of financial and electronic shares would determine whether the index could breach the 7,000-point barrier, brokers said.

The heavily weighted financials were strong in early session but encountered late profit-taking. The sector inched up 0.11 percent, with China Development Corp up T$2 or 2.27 percent to T$90. Most brokers agreed it would require a few days of consolidation before the index broke the key 7.000-point barrier again. A trading range of 6,850-6,950 was seen for Thursday. -- Alice Hung (2-5080815)
